gap: No result ChatGPT got states that today, on the makers' own US stores, the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-Port (X774) is $56.99 while Anker's 140W 4-Port with screen is $59.99, or that the Anker's own split table cuts each of two laptops on C1 and C2 to 70 W but keeps 100 W on C1 when a phone is on C3 (100 W + 40 W).
standout_why: I compared this against the cited Manuals+ A2697 guide, the B&H A2697 listing as quoted in ChatGPT's answer ('Two USB-C ports can supply 70W each together'), Macworld's Prime 250W and ChargeView 240W reviews, ChargerLAB's X774 teardown and UGREEN's Nexode Pro series page. Those pages already have the 70 W + 70 W figure and ChargerLAB's 98 W + 55 W reading. They do not have the Anker US price, the Anker table's 100 W + 40 W laptop-plus-phone row, or a side-by-side maker-store price for the two 140 W-tier display chargers. So this finding is partly new.
decides: This confirms our UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-Port as the pick for a wall charger in the 140 W tier with a per-port display. It costs less than the Anker A2697 at each maker's US store today ($56.99 against $59.99). ChargerLAB confirms its screen shows C1 and C2 watts at the same time and measured 98 W + 55 W with two devices. Anker's own US page only says the A2697 screen shows 'power, port status, and temperature'. The A2697 stays the better choice for one laptop plus a phone, where Anker's table keeps 100 W on the laptop port. For two laptops on a desk, the Satechi ChargeView 240W (100 W + 100 W per Macworld) and the Anker Prime 250W (up to 240 W across two ports) beat both, at about $149.99.
